author: claude
decision: Should we refinance our flat's mortgage with the new lender's lower-rate offer now, or keep the current loan?

options.label: Refinance with the new lender now

goal: Pay less in total over the next five years without taking on more risk.
constraints: The offer is valid for three weeks.
visible_context: The new lender offers a rate 1.1 points below our current one. Our broker estimated the fee for ending the current loan early at about one month of payments, which the savings recover within a year. We plan to stay in the flat for at least five years. Both loans are with well-known banks.

hidden_facts.text: The offered rate is fixed only for the first two years; after that it follows a variable index that is currently above our existing rate.
hidden_facts.why: Over five years the new loan is likely to cost more, and it adds rate risk the current loan does not have.
hidden_facts.how_to_learn: Read the rate section of the offer document, not the headline rate, and ask how the rate is set after the fixed period.

hidden_facts.text: The broker's estimate of the early-exit fee was based on the original loan amount; with the extra amount we borrowed last year, the actual fee is about five months of payments.
hidden_facts.why: The savings would take several years to recover the fee, which removes most of the gain.
hidden_facts.how_to_learn: Ask the current bank for a written early-repayment quote for the actual balance.

hidden_facts.text: The new lender's offer document is twelve pages long and also available in English.
hidden_facts.why: The length and language of the document do not change its terms.

hidden_facts.text: The broker has worked with our current bank for many years.
hidden_facts.why: The broker's relationship with the bank does not change the fee.

notes: Held out: written before pipeline v1 was run on any case.

author: claude
decision: Should I accept a senior engineering offer in Zurich and move there with my partner, or stay in my current job in Munich?

options.label: Accept the Zurich offer and move
Stay in my current job in Munich

goal: Take a real step up in responsibility within two years while my partner keeps their job.
constraints: I have to answer within ten days; the start date would be in three months.
visible_context: The offer pays about 40% more after accounting for the higher cost of living. The recruiter says the team is growing and the hiring manager wants me to lead a new subteam within a year. My partner's employer allows full remote work, so they can keep their job from Zurich. My current job is stable but there is no senior opening in sight.

hidden_facts.text: The hiring manager who promised the subteam has already resigned and leaves before my start date; the new subteam is not in next year's plan.
hidden_facts.why: The step up in responsibility, the main reason for moving, is unlikely to happen.
hidden_facts.how_to_learn: Ask to speak with someone on the team, or ask the hiring manager directly whether they will still be there and whether the subteam is in the budget.

hidden_facts.text: My partner's employer allows remote work only from within Germany, for tax and employment-law reasons.
hidden_facts.why: My partner would have to give up their job to move, which breaks the goal.
hidden_facts.how_to_learn: My partner asks their HR department in writing whether remote work from Switzerland is allowed.

hidden_facts.text: The hiring manager joined the company two years ago from a competitor.
hidden_facts.why: Where the manager came from says nothing about whether the promise will be kept.

hidden_facts.text: My partner's employer uses a different video-call tool than my future team.
hidden_facts.why: The tool does not affect whether my partner can work from Switzerland.

notes: Held out: written before pipeline v1 was run on any case.

author: claude
decision: Should we sign a ten-year lease for a second restaurant location on a busy street, or keep looking?

options.label: Sign the lease for this location

goal: Open a second location that is profitable within 18 months without putting the first one at risk.
constraints: The landlord wants an answer within two weeks; another tenant is interested.
visible_context: Our first restaurant is profitable and the menu works. The landlord's agent shared a pedestrian count showing much more foot traffic than at our first location. The rent is high but fits our plan if the traffic holds. The space was previously a clothing shop, so it needs a kitchen fit-out.

hidden_facts.text: The agent's pedestrian count was taken during the week of the street's annual festival.
hidden_facts.why: Normal traffic is likely far lower, so the high rent may not be covered.
hidden_facts.how_to_learn: Ask when the count was taken, or count yourself on ordinary weekdays and evenings.

hidden_facts.text: The building's owners' association does not permit an extraction duct through the roof or facade, which a cooking kitchen needs.
hidden_facts.why: We may not be able to run a full kitchen in the space at all, or only at a large extra cost.
hidden_facts.how_to_learn: Ask the landlord for the building rules and check with the city or a kitchen fitter whether ventilation can be approved.

hidden_facts.text: The agent's pedestrian count was made with a counting app on a phone.
hidden_facts.why: The counting method is fine for this purpose; when the count was made matters, not how.

hidden_facts.text: The building's facade was renovated three years ago.
hidden_facts.why: The renovation says nothing about whether a duct is allowed.

notes: Held out: written before pipeline v1 was run on any case.

author: claude
decision: Should we ship the new checkout in our shopping app two days before the holiday sale, or wait until after the sale?

options.label: Ship the new checkout before the sale

goal: Maximize sale-week revenue without a checkout outage.
constraints: The sale starts in nine days; the app stores need time to review the update.
visible_context: In the beta, the new checkout raised conversion by about 8%. The crash dashboard shows the beta build is as stable as the current one. The team plans to announce the sale with a push notification to all 2 million users at the start of the sale. Rolling back means shipping another app update.

hidden_facts.text: The crash dashboard does not include devices on the oldest supported OS version, which about a quarter of our customers use, because the crash reporting library does not support it.
hidden_facts.why: The new checkout's stability on a quarter of the user base is unknown, and a rollback during sale week is slow.
hidden_facts.how_to_learn: Check which OS versions the crash dashboard covers and test the new checkout on the oldest supported version.

hidden_facts.text: The beta testers were mostly staff and loyal customers who already had saved payment details.
hidden_facts.why: The 8% gain may not hold for the many first-time sale shoppers, so the upside of shipping early is smaller than it looks.
hidden_facts.how_to_learn: Look at who was in the beta and how the new checkout performed for users without saved payment details.

hidden_facts.text: The crash dashboard was redesigned last quarter with new charts.
hidden_facts.why: The new charts do not change which devices the data covers.

hidden_facts.text: The beta ran for three weeks.
hidden_facts.why: Three weeks is enough time; who was in the beta matters, not how long it ran.

notes: Held out: written before pipeline v1 was run on any case.
